record_quotes.text: ### 3b. Poor co-registration lock (offset > USBL bound or negative PSR)

Several pairs have horizontal offsets **> 30 m** (the AUV USBL bound) or **negative PSR** (ambiguous lock) — e.g. `KN210-05×22436` (offset 145 m), `EW9904×30217` (64 m), `FK006B×20811` (PSR −0.97), `FK171110×24485` (PSR −18). Deep, large, sparse-LR pairs co-register poorly; **the overlay must confirm the alignment** — a large solved offset may be a real USBL error correction or a bad lock. QGIS arbitrates.
3. **Scrutinize the large-offset/negative-PSR pairs (§3b)** — confirm real alignment vs bad lock.
| `clean` | **9** | horizontal lock good on real cells (offset ≤ 30 m USBL, PSR > 0) |
| `genuine_coreg_fail` | **14** | offset > 30 m or PSR ≤ 0 on real cells → QGIS scrutinize / likely exclude |
Lock quality is judged on the **horizontal** §3b criteria (offset within the AUV USBL
The 9 `clean` pairs lock within the USBL bound on real data (offset 2.7–16.7 m,

- **offset > 30 m** (most: FK181031×24620 59.7 m, TN299×31256 53.3 m, 2009_Amundsen 148.6 m, the SKQ/Tonga pairs ~47–53 m) — a solved shift beyond the AUV USBL bound: either a real large USBL error or a bad lock; **QGIS arbitrates**.
3. **14 coreg_fail (§4):** QGIS-arbitrate large-offset vs bad-lock via the `_overlay_f5`.

| **SantaMonica** `NA076×32317` | Santa Monica Mound (margin seep mound) | new | 50 | 4.1 | −862 / 866 ✓ | 47 m / 0.8 m | offset > 30 m USBL → **QGIS arbitrate** (MAD 0.8 m is excellent; same ~47–53 m offset the original NA076 pair showed) |

All three read real negative depths matching their sites; QC figures show matching HR/LR hillshades, shared-scale depth, small HR−LR diff over joint, and overlapping histograms. **Pescadero and Pythia lock cleanly within the USBL bound; Santa Monica's 47 m solved offset is the one judgment call** (a real USBL error vs a soft lock — the overlay is the arbiter, exactly as for the corpus's borderline pairs).
1. **Sign off the QC figures** (`c1_candidate__*.png`): I recommend advancing **Pescadero** and **Pythia** now; **Santa Monica** on your QGIS read of the 47 m offset.

- Harmonized the best sub-grid (`Shelf_Edge_Scar_w_Adj_Remnant`, 588k joint cells, full overlap): **144 tiles, −239 m, coreg offset 35 m / MAD 0.73**. Offset just over the 30 m USBL bound (like Santa Monica) → **QGIS read** — MAD 0.73 m is excellent.
| `NA076×32317` | Santa Monica Mound | continental_margin | 221 | 47.0 / 0.8 m | new lu; offset>USBL, QGIS-signed-off |
> `QGIS_R3_approved; PSR=undefined (no interior peak); offset=<X> m`

`coregister._residuals` and `qa.compute` already restrict to finite-in-both — but **re-run them on the `joint_valid` (real-data) mask**, not just `isfinite`, so §3b's bad locks (`KN210-05×22436` 145 m, `FK006B×20811` PSR −0.97, `FK171110×24485` PSR −18) are judged on real soundings, not interpolated fill. Verdict per pair: `clean` / `rescued` (locks once fill excluded) / `genuine_coreg_fail` (still poor → scrutinize/exclude).
